source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Only deep muscle and joint bleeding, identical to hemophilia, similar to what this client is currently assuming their own bleeding pattern will look like","B":"No bleeding tendency of any kind associated with this disorder, contrary to the actual bleeding risk this condition carries","C":"Excessive clotting with no associated bleeding risk, which describes the opposite of what this bleeding disorder actually causes","D":"Mucocutaneous bleeding, from impaired platelet adhesion, rather than the joint-and-muscle pattern seen in hemophilia that this client was asking about"}}
source_row.rationale: Von Willebrand disease, resulting from a deficiency or dysfunction of von Willebrand factor (important for platelet adhesion), typically presents with mucocutaneous bleeding patterns — such as easy bruising, frequent nosebleeds, bleeding gums, and heavy menstrual bleeding — distinct from the deep muscle/joint bleeding pattern more classically associated with hemophilia (a clotting factor deficiency).

source_row.stem: A client with von Willebrand disease, the most common inherited bleeding disorder, asks the nurse whether their bleeding pattern will look just like what they've read about hemophilia. The client would most likely instead present with which type of bleeding pattern?
